name: Thien Hau Temple
kicker: The sea goddess hall in Chợ Lớn
summary: Thiên Hậu is the temple the Chợ Lớn walk is for. Visit HCMC says the Cantonese community from Tuệ Thành county built it in 1760, and that the roof ceramics are from the Bửu Nguyên and Đồng Hòa kilns, year Mậu Thân 1908. The city itinerary and the southern page also call it Thiên Hậu Pagoda, the goddess of the sea. A street number was not printed. A fee was not printed.

notice.title: It is not Ngọc Hoàng or Giác Lâm
notice.body: Those are different halls, in different wards. Chùa Quan Âm, Hội quán Ôn Lăng, is the second hall on the same Visit HCMC page. No address for Quan Âm was printed, so it is not a separate stop.

body: Visit HCMC also calls the building Hội quán Tuệ Thành. The page says the incense set inside is the largest of the city’s temples. The feast days sit with the other events. An ordinary-day hour was not printed. District 5 is the city itinerary’s label. Chợ Lớn is the southern page’s label. Both stay.

The photograph is the street front: the ceramic roof, the gate, and the lanterns. The second photograph is the courtyard gate. The city itinerary puts the temple at the end of a Sunday that began at Tao Đàn and passed Chợ Tân Định. Minutes from the palace were not printed.
